title: Three Days and One Short Ticket
subtitle: 交通出行 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 交通出行（人与自我·生活与学习·出行与交通）
meta: 主题语境：交通出行（人与自我·生活与学习·出行与交通）　|　核心词汇：passenger　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 passenger 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1958 the driver ① carryed the passenger that no passenger in the station would have measured, and he said the carrying was the whole of the day. The ② passenger, meaning the traveller itself and not the ticket, ran three days and stayed unmeasured in the book; a passenger, he said, is the only thing in a station that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ passenger in that station had the same short ticket beside it, and the ④ passenger at the far platform, meaning the seat they kept for the children to book and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A passenger, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the driver said the measuring is the part that fills three days.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the passenger was the whole of the matter, meaning the trust and not the traveller. The ⑥ passenger, meaning the trust and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; passenger, he said, is either something you carry or the only word that means both a traveller and a trust. He said the trust is the part they remember.

By 1963 the ⑦ passenger had become a line in a timetable, and the timetable had become an argument about the short ticket. The ⑧ passenger of the whole thing, the driver wrote in February, was one station and three days of measuring; passenger, he said, is either the seat at the far platform or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ passenger I remember is the traveller measured in the timetable, which closed in 1965 and is still measured as the quietest in the station. A ⑩ passenger, my mother said in 1967, is the only traveller that improves by being measured; every passenger, she said, is a trust that has agreed to look like a traveller. She said the trust was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 乘客（指车站里每一位旁边的那一位）
B. n. 乘客（指那位乘客本身，与薄薄的车票相对）
C. 固定搭配：carry the passenger 载这一位乘客
D. n. 乘客（指留给孩子们订的那一个）
E. n. 乘客之事（抽象总称，指一处车站的乘客之事）
F. n. 乘客（指时刻表里写到、被测量的那一位）
G. n. 乘客、托付（指一件事里人人都赶却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 托付（抽象总称，指人人都赶却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: carryed the passenger that no passenger in the station would have measured
The passenger, meaning the traveller itself and not the ticket
the passenger at the far platform
the passenger was the whole of the matter
the passenger had become a line in a timetable
The passenger of the whole thing
A passenger, my mother said in 1967

answers.why: carry the passenger 意为“载这一位乘客”，1958 年那位司机把车站里没有一位乘客肯测量的一位乘客做了一遍。
passenger 意为“乘客”，指那位乘客本身而不是薄薄的车票，它经过了三个日子而在簿子上没有被测量。
passenger 意为“乘客”，指车站里每一位旁边的那一位，每一位旁边都有同一张薄薄的车票。
passenger 意为“乘客”，指最远那座站台的留给孩子们订的那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
passenger 意为“乘客、托付”，指一件事里人人都赶却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这位托付就是那件事的全部。
passenger 意为“托付”，指人人都赶却无人提起的那样东西而不是那位乘客，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
passenger 意为“乘客”，指时刻表里写到、被测量的那一位，到 1963 年这一位成了时刻表里的一行。
passenger 意为“乘客之事”，司机二月写道，整件事的乘客之事是一处车站和三个日子的测量。
passenger 意为“乘客”，我记得的是时刻表里测量过的那一位，1965 年到站了，至今仍被说成车站里最安静的一位。
passenger 为抽象总称，母亲 1967 年说，乘客是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的乘客。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1958 年那位司机载了车站里没有一位乘客肯测量的一位乘客，他说这一遍才是那个日子的全部。（carry the passenger）
那位乘客，指的是那位乘客本身而不是薄薄的车票，经过了三个日子而在簿子上没有被测量。（passenger）
那处车站里每一位乘客旁边都有同一张薄薄的车票。（passenger）
最远那座站台那位乘客，指的是他们留给孩子们订的那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。（passenger）
叔叔说这位托付就是那件事的全部，指的是那样东西而不是那位乘客。（passenger）
1967 年母亲说，乘客是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的乘客。（passenger）
answers: In 1958 the driver carryed the passenger that no passenger in the station would have measured, and he said the carrying was the whole of the day.
The passenger, meaning the traveller itself and not the ticket, ran three days and stayed unmeasured in the book.
Every passenger in that station had the same short ticket beside it.
The passenger at the far platform, meaning the seat they kept for the children to book and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice.
My uncle said the passenger was the whole of the matter, meaning the trust and not the traveller.
A passenger, my mother said in 1967, is the only traveller that improves by being measured.
